resources.string: Live audio, captions and text input

Starting sends thread/realtime/start for this thread. A client that can do WebRTC attaches an SDP offer built from a peer connection that already carries the realtime events data channel; this build creates no peer connection, so it sends no offer and the server applies its own transport.

Nothing has been requested from this page. Whether a session is live is what thread/realtime/started, thread/realtime/closed and thread/realtime/error report, and those notifications are not read here — so this is the page\'s own state, not the server\'s.

This records only that the request was sent. thread/realtime/started would confirm the session came up and thread/realtime/error would refuse it; neither is folded into this page, so the button can be out of step with the server.

Captions stream from thread/realtime/transcript/delta, thread/realtime/transcript/done and thread/realtime/item/transcript/delta onto the event flow the app-level reducer owns, which is where a transcript belongs: it has to outlive this page. This build folds none of them yet and the page is never handed the client, so live captions appear on the transcript surface and not here.
thread/realtime/listVoices has not answered for this server, or it offers none. Reload above asks again.
A voice is chosen when a session starts and no call sets one afterwards: thread/realtime/listVoices only enumerates them. Tapping a row moves the tick on this page and sends nothing.
Type what you would otherwise say
thread/realtime/appendText adds a conversation item to the live session. With the protocol\'s default role that is the user typing instead of speaking, so it is input the model answers.
thread/realtime/appendSpeech hands the server text this client produced and asks for it to be voiced. It is not a user turn, the model does not answer it, and nothing about it is transcribed back.

Audio reaches a session as one ThreadRealtimeAudioChunk per push through thread/realtime/appendAudio: PCM samples in base64 data, a channel count, a sample rate, and optionally the transcript item the audio belongs to.

No recorder is bound in this build: nothing constructs an AudioRecord, so no frame is read and no chunk is ever built. A working capture would read PCM frames and push them as chunks; here the button moves this page\'s own flag and nothing else.

The flag is on and nothing is being captured: with no AudioRecord behind it there are no frames, no chunks and no call to thread/realtime/appendAudio. That is what a capture indicator has to say when there is nothing to indicate.
